title: service-account-rotation-and-k8s-tenant-separation-notes
content:
Context and scope:
- Purpose: capture a pragmatic on-prem playbook for rotating control-plane/service-account credentials and splitting tenant workloads into separated namespaces/tenants for regulatory customers. Target platforms: bare-metal (PXE/IPMI) fleets and vSphere-hosted customer clusters (airgapped and VPC-connected variants).
- Audience: field engineering, private-deployments oncall, SRE handoff. This is a working doc: rough step sequences, Terraform module interaction notes, and a phased upgrade/rollback plan.
- Goals: minimize downtime, preserve API stability for customers, maintain auditability (rotate keys with logged attestations), and allow incremental cutover of tenants.

Quick summary of approach:
1) Prepare infra and telemetry: ensure rollout feature-flags in console + metrics tagging for tenant/cluster, and enable extra retention for audit logs for the rotation window.
2) Add terraform hooks to stage new service-account objects (K8s ServiceAccounts + bound secrets) and KMS-wrapped keys; apply in a non-destructive, idempotent way.
3) Canary: pick 1 small cluster or 1 tenant namespace to validate credential rotation flows (API calls, webhook auth, CSI drivers).
4) Tenant separation: move workloads into new namespaces/NetworkPolicies and update RBAC bindings to use the new SA identities.
5) Controlled rolling upgrade/drain of nodes (respecting stateful sets): coordinate pod disruption budgets and long-lived connections.
6) Cutover and revoke old keys after 48–72h of stable telemetry.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any cluster apply):
- Backup etcd snapshot verified and stored offsite (at least 2 copies).
- Terraform state locked and terraform plan reviewed.
- BMC/IPMI console accessible for bare metal nodes (serial-over-LAN smoke tests).
- vSphere snapshot policy defined for control-plane VMs (if vSphere) + quick rollback play.
- Kubelet and kube-apiserver metrics ingestion verified; request tracing configured for the window.
- RBAC audit: list of current ClusterRoles/Bindings for affected SAs exported.
- CSI and external-auth drivers compatibility matrix confirmed (some drivers read tokens directly).
- Support rotation runbook briefed to oncall team and customers (if required).

Terraform module notes (observations / TODOs):
- Module: modules/k8s-service-account (existing) needs a new boolean var: rotate_in_place (default: false). If true, module should create new serviceaccount with suffix -rot{timestamp} and output both identities.
- Module should expose outputs: service_account_name, secret_name, k8s_sa_uid, iam_binding_id (for cloud-integrations). All outputs are strings.
- State handling: create resources as separate objects (non-destructive). Avoid in-place replacement of secrets. Plan should show adds then safe deletes after verification.
- Backend: remote state bucket must have versioning enabled. Add pre-apply hook that uploads the current terraform plan to the audit S3/GCS bucket.
- Idempotency: ensure apply is safe when re-run; use lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true } for secrets/roles where possible.
- Locking: enforce a single operator apply per-cluster via a small mutex object in a central state repo (or use dynamodb/locker).
- Example variables to add to cluster module: 
  - sa_rotation_window (string) e.g., "48h"
  - break_glacier_backup (bool) to force extra snapshots pre-rotate
  - tenant_migration_mode: ["none","shadow","cutover"]
- Notes on provider constraints: on airgapped installs we cannot rely on cloud IAM APIs. Module should support a KMS adapter that materializes wrapped keys into Secrets (k8s sealed-secrets pattern) created via offline tooling.

Canary and rollout plan (detailed):
Phase A – Preparation (T-72 to T-24)
- T-72: run full etcd snapshot + verify restoration in a dry-run cluster.
- T-48: apply terraform plan in a staging copy of the cluster or a dev-fleet. Validate generated SA tokens, secret mounts, and webhook auth.
- T-36: tag telemetry: enable tenant=canary tag for test namespace. Confirm all alerts are silenced for this window except critical control-plane alarms.

Phase B – Canary (T-24 to T+48)
- T-24: create new SA via terraform with "rotate_in_place=true" semantics for the canary tenant. Deploy a mirrored service that authenticates with both old+new tokens (shadow path).
- Monitor: API latency, 401/403 rates, webhook failures, CSI mounts. Collect logs for any auth-related errors.
- After 12–24h of stable operation, move a small percentage (5–10%) of traffic to the new SA identity using a weighted traffic rule in the service mesh (if present) or DNS-based cutover.

Phase C – Tenant separation and bulk rollout (T+48 to T+7d)
- Convert tenant namespaces to use new SA in manifests; keep old SA secrets present but not used.
- For stateful components (DBs), run connection draining by application-level handoff (session draining) before kube drain.
- Use node-level cordon + drain with maxUnavailable configured; on bare metal increase drain timeout to allow in-place PV detach/attach (use --grace-period and --timeout options).

Phase D – Revoke and cleanup (after T+72 with stable telemetry)
- Run a final pass: kube delete secret <old-secret> but keep a recorded snapshot of its value in the audit store encrypted by KMS.
- Revoke old tokens at the control-plane auth layer (or rotate the OIDC client secret if used).
- Update Confluence with attestations and link to the terraform plan used.

Rollback plan (if canary shows regressions):
- Immediately switch traffic back to old SA path (service mesh weighted rule or DNS TTL-based rollback).
- Reapply old RBAC bindings if any were changed.
- If secrets were deleted, restore from snapshot store. Use the stored etcd snapshot to recover deleted secret values if needed (last resort).
- If control-plane instability: rollback vSphere VM snapshot or re-deploy control-plane with previous kube-apiserver args preserved.

Edge-case operational notes (uncomfortable but real):
- Bare metal NIC flip: if node NIC rewriting is involved, drains can take >15m due to iSCSI/long PV detach. Plan 2x time budget and coordinate BMC ATX for force restart windows.
- Airgap: sealed secrets and manual key wrapping must be rehearsed — include a local KMS-wrapper utility (scripts/wrap-key.sh) and store wrapped payloads in the cluster-assets repo before start.
- CSI drivers often cache tokens: ensure driver restart/rolling update post-rotation to pick up new secrets (explicitly document which drivers require restart).
- Admission controllers and webhooks: some controllers call external APIs that rely on SA tokens; add a pre-check to call each webhook endpoint with new token in staging.

Telemetry & Audit additions to enable for the window:
- Increase APIserver audit log verbosity by 1 level for the rotation window and push to long-term storage.
- Add metric: k8s.sa.rotation.status{cluster,tenant,sa}=ok|degraded|revoked. Emit this metric from the rotation operator wrap.
- Add alert: >5% of auth failures post-rotation for 10m -> paging.
- Record terraform plan object and attach to the ticket (JIRA-INF-4382) before apply.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to safely rotate tokens for long-lived external services (e.g., Prometheus remote write, third-party DB connectors) without double-secret-sourcing the config? Can we support a dual-read config pattern? TODO @Priya to prototype.
- Decide retention policy for archived old secrets in audit store (30d vs 90d). Compliance asks for 90d but storage ops prefer 30d.
- Need a small utility that can detect which CSI drivers and webhook pods mount SA tokens directly (static list is brittle). TODO: Diego to spike.
- Confirm if vSphere snapshots can be taken while control-plane components are cert-rotating; some environments have snapshot quiesce issues.

Quick runbook (one-page version):
1) Alert oncall and create run ticket.
2) Run etcd backup and verify.
3) Terraform plan -> upload plan artifact -> apply in canary cluster.
4) Start canary namespace with dual tokens; run smoke tests.
5) Wait 24h stable; run 5–10% traffic cutover.
6) If green, schedule bulk rollout in waves of 10–20% tenants per 6–8 hours with increased monitoring.
7) After 72h stable, revoke old keys and record attestation.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep an eye on kube-controller-manager logs for token review errors — those popup often when RBAC tweaks are incomplete.
- During last test a node-level iSCSI leak caused 3 pods to stall during drain; adding a pre-drain lsof check reduced failures.
- Remember: for airgapped, we must not depend on external 3rd-party token validation services.

References and quick links:
- Internal: Confluence rotation doc (linked above)
- PR: terraform-modules/#351 (service-account rotate feature)
- JIRA: INF-4382 (Runbook + Postmortem)

If you iterate on this doc: add steps you test to the bottom under "test evidence" with timestamps and short results.

End of draft.
